cues.en: Red teaming is another way that'll evaluations are done.
cues.zh: 紅隊測試，是另一種 LLM 評估方式。

cues.en: It's kind of like black box evaluations, but scaled up to be more targeted, more adversarial and more professional.
cues.zh: 有點像黑箱評估，但規模更大、更有針對性、更具對抗性，也更專業。

cues.en: In fact, I will introduce and explain what red teaming means by contrasting it with black box evals.
cues.zh: 我會透過與黑箱評估對照，解釋紅隊的意思。

cues.en: So red teaming is usually more targeted and focused on specific risks, including safety or privacy
cues.zh: 紅隊通常更聚焦特定風險，包括安全、隱私

cues.en: concerns, whereas black box evals tend to be more focused on bias and fairness, or just people's curiosity
cues.zh: 問題；黑箱評估則常著重偏見、公平，或單純出於好奇，

cues.en: to see if they can outsmart the AI and the engineers who put the guardrails on the AI.
cues.zh: 看看能否智取 AI，以及設置防護的工程師。

cues.en: Red teaming is a professional activity that is done by trained security experts who often have a background in computer science, technology, or cybersecurity.
cues.zh: 紅隊是專業活動，由受訓的資安專家執行，常有電腦科學、科技或網路安全背景。

cues.en: While black box evals are often done by researchers and curious users, and is often done as a hobby
cues.zh: 黑箱評估則常由研究者、好奇的使用者進行，作為興趣、

cues.en: or like a curious exploration, and not so much as a full time profession.
cues.zh: 探索，而不是全職專業。

cues.en: Black box evals literally, by definition, do not have access to any of the internals of the model.
cues.zh: 依定義，黑箱完全無法存取模型內部。

cues.en: Red teaming, on the other hand, is sometimes black box only.
cues.zh: 但紅隊有時只有黑箱，

cues.en: But for example, if an AI development company hires a security team to do a red team assessment on
cues.zh: 例如，AI 公司聘安全團隊，對自家

cues.en: their WL, then the company will probably give the security team at least some access to the model's
cues.zh: LLM 做紅隊評估，可能會提供一些

cues.en: internals, and maybe also some information about the training data sets, the system prompts, other guardrails, and so on.
cues.zh: 內部存取權，也許還有訓練集、系統提示詞、防護機制資訊。

cues.en: Because red teaming is usually more targeted for a particular security risk, or a privacy vulnerability
cues.zh: 因為較聚焦特定安全風險、隱私漏洞，

cues.en: tends to be more professional, and the the techniques tend to be a little bit more aggressive, more
cues.zh: 也較專業，技術往往更積極、

cues.en: adversarial, and may also include attempts to hack the model or hack into the server that the model is on.
cues.zh: 更具對抗性，可能包含嘗試駭入模型，或模型所在伺服器。

cues.en: In some cases, it might also involve social engineering to hack into the developers, the humans who
cues.zh: 有時也包含社交工程，測試開發者、

cues.en: to see if there are security risks not just of the model itself, but the employees who are supposed to physically safeguard the model.
cues.zh: 人員的風險，不只看模型，還看負責保護模型的員工。

cues.en: And for the same reasons, red teaming tends to be a little bit more rigorous and methodical, whereas
cues.zh: 同樣原因，紅隊通常更嚴謹、有系統；

cues.en: a lot of black box evals are done by individuals or perhaps research groups.
cues.zh: 許多黑箱評估由個人，或研究團隊進行，

cues.en: And so it's a little bit more informal.
cues.zh: 比較非正式。

cues.en: Perhaps one way to understand this is that imagine you are working at an AI company, and you want to make sure that your language models are safe and secure.
cues.zh: 可以這樣理解：假設在 AI 公司工作，希望模型安全可靠，

cues.en: You would hire a professional security company to red team your model, whereas any flaws identified
cues.zh: 會聘專業資安公司做紅隊；而黑箱評估發現的

cues.en: by black box evals would come maybe from your developers or from your users after you've released the model.
cues.zh: 缺陷，可能來自開發者，或模型發布後的使用者。

cues.en: Now there are some red team groups that have published some of their attempts.
cues.zh: 有些紅隊公開過嘗試。

cues.en: I thought about pasting some of them into this lecture, but too many of those dialogues with the models
cues.zh: 我曾想把一些對話放進課程，但太多內容

cues.en: involve trying to get the models to agree with some really awful sexist or racist comments, or to try
cues.zh: 涉及誘導模型認同糟糕的性別、種族歧視言論，或

cues.en: to get the model to give instructions for, for example, how to buy or sell drugs on the dark web or other topics like that.
cues.zh: 要求提供暗網買賣毒品等指示。

cues.en: So I decided that I do not want to include that kind of language directly in this course.
cues.zh: 所以決定，不直接在課程放這些話。

cues.en: But if you are curious, you can read through some of the red team attempts that you can find online.
cues.zh: 但如果好奇，可以閱讀網路公開的紅隊嘗試。

cues.en: For example, you can look here on the Hugging Face site for anthropic.
cues.zh: 例如 Hugging Face 的 Anthropic 頁面，

cues.en: Here is their red team attempts.
cues.zh: 這是他們的紅隊資料。

cues.en: This is their harmless and helpful data sets, which we have actually looked at a little bit in the previous section.
cues.zh: 也就是 harmless、helpful 資料集，上一章已簡單看過。

cues.en: And also if you just search around online, you can find some other human computer dialogues that have been used in red teaming.
cues.zh: 另外上網找，也能找到其他紅隊用過的人機對話。

cues.en: So that's a brief description of red teaming.
cues.zh: 以上是紅隊簡介。

cues.en: Again, it's a super important area for the safety of AI, but this is all I'm going to say about it in this course.
cues.zh: 同樣，它對 AI 安全非常重要，但這門課就介紹到這裡。
